doc.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Whether Boston Latin was integrated
summary: Almost no black students then; he notes later desegregation and the separate Girls Latin School.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: To go back to Boston Latin just for one quick moment: was that an integrated school? Were there black students?

No, there were very few blacks then. That took a lot of doing. That happened when finally the Supreme Court said that in public schools, segregated education was inherently unconstitutional. Then Boston became a storm center there. But eventually, when I come back there now, there are a lot of black kids and a lot – girls couldn’t go. It was like an orthodox synagogue, where the women had to sit up in the balcony. There was a Girls Latin School across the street. That no longer exists. It’s integrated.
